# Treemaps {#sec-treemaps} ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"} ## Theme: `theme_j2me()` Graphs in this chapter use `fmggp2::theme_j2me()`, built from a Nokia N73 running a J2ME app: a black phone background, a silver frame, a pale screen panel, Ushahidi red, tan, brown, and black marks, and an Arial Narrow title. ::: :::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}
::: {.cell layout-align="right"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](treemaps_files/figure-html/full_code_display-1.png){fig-align='right' width=60% height=60%} ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"} **Requirements:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ at least two categorical variables** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a numeric variable of counts (for each level of the categorical variables)** ::: :::: ## Description A treemap shows how one whole breaks into parts, and how each part breaks into smaller parts, as boxes set inside one big box.[^hierarchy] The size of each box shows how much of the whole that part takes up.[^area] The boxes are kept about as high as they are wide,[^squarified] so their sizes are easy to compare. We'll make a treemap with the code in [`treemapify`](http://wilkox.org/treemapify/).[^treemapify-pkg] Mosaic plots also show the parts of a whole as boxes (see @sec-mosaic-plots). ## Set up ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **PACKAGES:** ::: Bring in the code we'll use.[^packages] ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} # pak::pak("wilkox/treemapify") library(treemapify) library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) # for tibble() and data manipulation library(tidyr) # for expand_grid() ``` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DATA:** ::: J2ME was a way to write small programs, like games, that could run on many kinds of phones.[^j2me] From 2000 to about 2007, most phone games were J2ME games. A download is one time a phone gets a game through the air.[^ota] The deck was the games page that the phone company put on each phone.[^deck] People most often paid for each download on the deck. J2ME games were used until newer phones with their own game stores took their place.[^app-stores] We'll make up[^simulate] one year of downloads for six made up games of three kinds: puzzle, racing, and sports.[^genres] Each game gets a `yearly_rate` (how many downloads we'd expect in a year) and a `deck_share` (the part of those downloads bought on the deck instead of straight from the site of the company that made the game).[^publisher] `tidyr::expand_grid()` makes a row for each game and each way to buy it (`channel`),[^channel] `lambda` breaks the rate for the year into one part for each way to buy, and `rpois()` picks the downloads.[^draw] Starting with `set.seed()`[^seed] means you'll get the same downloads every time you run the code below. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} set.seed(2003) # same downloads every time the code runs j2me_downloads <- tibble( genre = c("Puzzle", "Puzzle", "Racing", "Racing", # three genres, two games each "Sports", "Sports"), title = c("Block Drop", "Gem Swap", "Street Rally", "Moto Sprint", # six games "Pocket Soccer", "Pro Bowling"), yearly_rate = c(1800, 900, 2400, 700, 1200, 1000), # average downloads per year deck_share = c(0.80, 0.40, 0.35, 0.60, 0.55, 0.50) # share sold through the carrier's menu ) |> tidyr::expand_grid(channel = c("Carrier deck", "Direct")) |> # each game in both channels mutate( lambda = yearly_rate * if_else(channel == "Carrier deck", deck_share, 1 - deck_share), # average downloads in each channel downloads = rpois(n(), lambda = lambda) # download counts around each average ) |> select(genre, title, channel, lambda, downloads) glimpse(j2me_downloads) #> Rows: 12 #> Columns: 5 #> $ genre "Puzzle", "Puzzle", "Puzzle", … #> $ title "Block Drop", "Block Drop", "G… #> $ channel "Carrier deck", "Direct", "Car… #> $ lambda 1440, 360, 360, 540, 840, 1560… #> $ downloads 1493, 346, 387, 539, 849, 1549… ``` ::: ::: ## Distribution A count is how many times something happens. A treemap puts counts inside counts:[^nest] ways to buy inside games, and games inside kinds of game. The size of each box is a part of all the downloads,[^tile-area] so the question behind the graph is "how much of the whole does each piece take up?" Below we'll move from the downloads, to a graph, to the rule behind it.[^formula] ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **COUNT IT:** ::: Start with the rows for Block Drop and Street Rally, two of the six games we made up. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} j2me_downloads |> filter(title %in% c("Block Drop", "Street Rally")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: Each made up count (`downloads`) lands within a few parts in 100[^percent] of the rate we gave `rpois()` (`lambda`). Block Drop got most of its downloads on the deck, while Street Rally got most of its downloads straight from the company that made it. Adding up the counts inside each kind of game gives the total for that kind. Each total, as a part of all the downloads, is the size of its box in the treemap.[^shares] ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} j2me_downloads |> group_by(genre) |> summarise(downloads = sum(downloads), expected = sum(lambda)) |> mutate(share = round(downloads / sum(downloads), 3)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DRAW IT:** ::: A bar model shows the groups one step at a time.[^levels] Each kind of game is a bar, each game is a part of its kind's bar, and each part has two colors, one for each way to buy. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} ggplot(j2me_downloads, aes(x = downloads, y = title, fill = channel)) + geom_col() + facet_grid(genre ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") + labs(x = "Downloads", y = NULL, fill = "Channel") + theme(legend.position = "bottom") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](treemaps_files/figure-html/draw_bar_model_treemap-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: A treemap takes the same parts and puts them all inside one box.[^rectangle] Below, the lighter lines go around each kind of game, the black lines go around each game,[^borders] and the red and light brown colors show the two ways to buy each game. The Block Drop box is almost all deck downloads, and most of the Street Rally box is downloads straight from the company that made it. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} ggplot(j2me_downloads, aes(area = downloads, fill = channel, subgroup = genre, subgroup2 = title)) + treemapify::geom_treemap() + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_border(color = "#15110E", size = 3) + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_text(color = "#FFFFFF", place = "center", min.size = 0, family = "sans") + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_border(color = "#9A9791", size = 6) + labs(fill = "Channel") + theme(legend.position = "bottom") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](treemaps_files/figure-html/draw_treemap-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **NAME IT:** ::: Each count for one game and one way to buy comes from [a rule for how many times something happens at a set rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisson_distribution):[^poisson-tm] $$ N_{\text{title, channel}} \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda_{\text{title, channel}}) $$ Counts from this rule do something good for treemaps: when we add counts that each come about on their own,[^independent] the total follows the same rule, and its rate is the total of their rates.[^additive] So the total for each kind of game follows $\text{Poisson}(\sum \lambda)$: 2,700 for puzzle, 3,100 for racing, and 2,200 for sports. Under this rule, how far a count usually falls from its rate is $\sqrt{\lambda}$,[^poisson-sd] so how far it moves as a part of the rate is $\sqrt{\lambda} / \lambda = 1 / \sqrt{\lambda}$.[^cv] For the Block Drop deck box ($\lambda = 1{,}440$) that's less than 3 in 100, which is why the boxes in the treemap change form very little each time we make up the data again. Try making every `yearly_rate` 100 times smaller, and the small boxes start to move around a lot. ## Grammar ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **CODE:** ::: - Make the words around the graph[^labels] with `labs()` - Start the graph with `ggplot()` and give it `data` - Join[^map] `downloads` to `area`, `channel` to `fill` and `label`, `genre` to `subgroup`, and `title` to `subgroup2` - Add `geom_treemap()` - Add `geom_treemap_text()` - `place`: this sets where the boxes start - `color`: the color of the words - `min.size`: the smallest the letters can get[^font-size] (when the words change size to fit) - `alpha`: how much the words cover what is behind them[^opacity] - `fontface`: `itlalic`/`bond` - `family`: `"sans"`/`"sansserif"`/`"mono"` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} labs_treemap <- labs( title = "J2ME downloads 2005", caption = "Simulated data", fill = "Channel") ggp2_treemap <- ggplot(j2me_downloads, aes(area = downloads, fill = channel, label = channel, subgroup = genre, subgroup2 = title)) + treemapify::geom_treemap() + treemapify::geom_treemap_text( place = "bottomright", color = "#FFFFFF", min.size = 0, alpha = 0.90, fontface = "italic", family = "sans") ggp2_treemap + labs_treemap ``` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"} **GRAPH:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell layout-nrow="1"} ```{.r .cell-code} labs_treemap <- labs( title = "J2ME downloads 2005", caption = "Simulated data", fill = "Channel") ggp2_treemap <- ggplot(j2me_downloads, aes(area = downloads, fill = channel, label = channel, subgroup = genre, subgroup2 = title)) + treemapify::geom_treemap() + treemapify::geom_treemap_text( place = "bottomright", color = "#FFFFFF", min.size = 0, alpha = 0.90, fontface = "italic", family = "sans") ggp2_treemap + labs_treemap ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](treemaps_files/figure-html/create_graph_treemap-1.png){width=100% height=100%} ::: ::: ::: ## More info `treemapify` has many choices for making treemaps.[^options] We cover a few of these below, but you should read the [long example that comes with it](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/treemapify/vignettes/introduction-to-treemapify.html).[^vignette] ### Subgroup The deepest groups are the smallest ones inside, and the shallowest are the biggest ones that hold the others. `ggplot2` puts each part of the graph down in the order it's written,[^layer-order] so the makers of `treemapify` [say](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/treemapify/vignettes/introduction-to-treemapify.html) to add the groups inside groups[^subgroups] "*from deepest to shallowest*", with `subgroups2` first (ending on `subgroup`) - Add `geom_treemap_subgroup2_border()` - Set the `size` and `color` - Add `geom_treemap_subgroup2_text()` - `place`: this sets where the boxes start - `color`: the color of the words - `min.size`: the smallest the letters can get (when the words change size to fit) - `alpha`: how much the words cover what is behind them - `fontface`: `itlalic`/`bond` - `family`: `"sans"`/`"sansserif"`/`"mono"` See the full list of choices[^arguments] [here](http://wilkox.org/treemapify/). ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell layout-nrow="1"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggp2_tm_subgroup <- ggp2_treemap + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_border( color = "#15110E", size = 4.0) + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup2_text( place = "center", alpha = 0.75, color = "#FFFFFF", min.size = 0, family = "sans") ggp2_tm_subgroup + labs_treemap ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](treemaps_files/figure-html/code_graph_treemap_sgb-1.png){width=100% height=100%} ::: ::: ::: ### Subgroup 2 - Add `geom_treemap_subgroup_border()` - Set the `size` and `color` - Add `geom_treemap_subgroup_text()` - `place`: this sets where the boxes start - `color`: the color of the words - `min.size`: the smallest the letters can get (when the words change size to fit) - `alpha`: how much the words cover what is behind them - `fontface`: `itlalic`/`bond` - `family`: `"sans"`/`"sansserif"`/`"mono"` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell layout-nrow="1"} ```{.r .cell-code} ggp2_tm_subgroup2 <- ggp2_tm_subgroup + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_border( color = "#9A9791", size = 4) + treemapify::geom_treemap_subgroup_text( place = "topleft", alpha = 0.65, grow = TRUE, color = "#FFFFFF", min.size = 0, family = "mono", fontface = "bold") ggp2_tm_subgroup2 + labs_treemap ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](treemaps_files/figure-html/code_graph_tmap_sgb_2-1.png){width=100% height=100%} ::: ::: ::: [^hierarchy]: Treemaps display a hierarchy of categorical variables as proportionally divided, nested rectangles. [^area]: Each tile's area is proportional to its value, so it shows that level's relative contribution to the total. [^squarified]: The squarified layout keeps the aspect ratio of each tile close to 1. [^treemapify-pkg]: The `treemapify` package, which adds treemap geoms to `ggplot2`. [^packages]: Install and load the packages. [^j2me]: Java 2 Platform, Micro Edition (J2ME, later Java ME). Mobile games were packaged as MIDP MIDlets. [^ota]: Downloaded over the air (OTA) through the mobile network. [^deck]: The carrier deck: the games menu on the carrier's (mobile operator's) portal. [^app-stores]: The iPhone App Store and Android Market (both 2008). [^simulate]: Simulate. [^genres]: Genres. [^publisher]: Bought directly from the publisher's site. [^channel]: The sales channel ("Carrier deck" or "Direct"). [^draw]: `rpois()` draws a random count from a Poisson distribution with rate `lambda`. [^seed]: Setting the random seed. [^nest]: Nested counts: channels inside titles, and titles inside genres. [^tile-area]: Every tile's area is a share of the total downloads. [^formula]: The formula. [^percent]: A few percent. [^shares]: Dividing each genre total by the overall total gives the shares (proportions) the treemap draws. [^levels]: The hierarchy, one level at a time. [^rectangle]: One rectangle. [^borders]: The subgroup borders: silver (`#9A9791`) outlines the genres and black (`#15110E`) outlines the titles. [^poisson-tm]: A Poisson distribution, which gives the number of times something happens in a fixed interval when it happens at a constant average rate. [^independent]: Independent Poisson counts. [^additive]: The sum of independent Poisson counts is also Poisson, with a rate equal to the sum of the rates. [^poisson-sd]: The standard deviation of a Poisson count is $\sqrt{\lambda}$. [^cv]: The relative variation (coefficient of variation), $1 / \sqrt{\lambda}$. [^labels]: The labels (title, caption, and legend title). [^map]: Map the variables to aesthetics in `aes()`. [^font-size]: The minimum font size. [^opacity]: Opacity. [^options]: Options. [^vignette]: The package vignette. [^layer-order]: `ggplot2` builds layers in the order they're written. [^subgroups]: Subgroups. [^arguments]: Arguments.
